note.question: How do discretionary service lines shape design and pricing?
note.overview: For discretionary services, longer service duration implies higher service quality. This paper studies the optimal design and pricing of discretionary service lines, a range of services that are vertically differentiated through their duration (quality), offered to a market with customers who are heterogeneous in terms of their sensitivity to service duration. In a resource-constrained environment with stochastic arrival of demand, longer service duration also implies longer wait, which all customers dislike.
